{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Tex-Mex cuisine|Tex-Mex Cuisine]]

This '''cheese enchilada''' recipe was handed down from the grandmother and mother of the original contributor.  

==Ingredients==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:flour|flour]]
* 3 tbsp [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|chili powder]]
* 3 tbsp [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|vegetable oil]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:water|water]]
* 1½ [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] (680 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) grated [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar cheese]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* ~20 corn [[Cookbook:tortilla|tortillas]]

==Procedure==
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (175°C).
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] chili powder and flour in oil in a 10–12-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (25–30 cm) skillet until emulsified. Add water, bring to a [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]], and then stir for ~5 minutes until slightly thickened. Turn down heat to low.
# Soak one tortilla in the chili gravy until softened (20–30 seconds). Remove tortilla from gravy, place flat on a plate, and add ~1 tbsp cheese and ~1 tbsp onion to center of the tortilla. Roll it up, and place with edges facing down in a 9 x 12-inch (23 x 30 cm) baking pan. Repeat this until you have used all the tortillas. If you get low on the gravy at the end, stir in ⅛–¼ cup of water.
# Cover the enchiladas with the remaining cheese, onions, and chili gravy.
# Bake in oven for about 5 minutes—longer will toughen the cheese.
# Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* These freeze well, but defrost completely before reheating.
* In Tex-Mex cuisine, these are often served with [[Cookbook:Mexican Rice|Mexican rice]], pinto beans, and guacamole salad.
